purpose: Propose the first Ashen Thrones Gameplay Benchmark corpus, scoring rubric, execution model, and cadence for player-AI-DM communication. Design only. No corpus adoption, runner, scorer, provider call, or gameplay change.
executive_summary: Implementation outcome: a reviewable ATGB-01 design, a 10-scenario catalog of 37 scored turns, and a feasibility note that reuses chat, isolated storage, and the existing evidence packet. No production code, test, evaluator, or runner was added. Original reproduction: not applicable; this pass repairs no gameplay failure. Related generalization: not applicable. Independent generalization: not evaluated. Regression: not run; no product or test change. ATGB: no result. The corpus is proposed and is not adopted, so the evidence standard still forbids an ATGB claim. Known limitations: Frontier Gate facts and the current conversational owners bound the scenarios; held-out wording is visible in this review package so reviewers can judge it, and it is not yet in a reserved directory. Remaining uncertainty: adoption, trial count, held-out location, the live-call budget, and whether S07 should move into the reserved slice are open. No gameplay improvement is claimed. Deterministic success is not proposed as evidence of natural conversation.

validation: No test, evaluator, threshold, calibration case, protected replay, or playability scenario changed. evaluate_playability remains the playability contract and is not an ATGB verdict.
tooling: No runner, scorer, or review-generator change. The existing ZIP sections carry the proposal, the unrun benchmark, and the open decisions.

testing.new_regressions: None. No production or test change.
testing.pre_existing_failures: Not reassessed. The PR-BL session orientation remains unreconciliation with later PR-EG history.

decisions_requiring_human_review: Adopt or reject ATGB-01 as the reviewed corpus. Until adoption, no Ashen Thrones Gameplay Benchmark result may be claimed.
Confirm Frontier Gate as the benchmark world.
Confirm human rubric scoring, with playability output allowed only as adjacent telemetry.
Confirm the reserved location data/validation/atgb/held_out/ and the rule that implementation work does not load or quote it.
Choose one live trial or three for the first baseline, and set the provider-call budget.
Decide whether a generic OOC acknowledgement that misses the question fails response success. The proposal says it does.
Decide whether S07 stays development-visible or moves to held-out.
Decide whether efficiency remains recorded-only in rubric 01.
The NEXT_SESSION versus PR-EG orientation discrepancy is a separate maintenance item. This package does not decide it.

campaign_specific: The corpus is not adopted. Reconsideration before adoption cannot produce an ATGB result and does not authorize a provider call.
Held-out player lines are included in the review catalog so suitability can be judged. They are not yet isolated from ordinary implementation context.
S09 does not require a two-NPC conversation system; a single clarification is the successful path. A future implementer could mistake that scenario for a crowd-simulation request.
docs/NEXT_SESSION.md product orientation remains the 2026-09-26 PR-BL closeout. Later PR-EG history remains in handoff history. This design records that discrepancy and does not reconcile it.
pre_existing: Playability scoring, semantic calibration, protected replay, and replay failure classification keep their existing authorities.

Curfew hours, stew price, diegetic time passage, compound multi-action execution, and richer pronoun continuity remain outside current authored behavior. The catalog treats grounded uncertainty or one clarification as success.

missing_concepts: An adopted ATGB corpus, an isolated-store driver, and a human judgment sheet. None is implemented here.
A provider price table. Future reports must say cost is unavailable when telemetry has no priced token counts.
The review generator has no dedicated ATGB fields. This package uses the existing summary sections.
does_not_prove: An Ashen Thrones Gameplay Benchmark result, a host-lane result, or a live-provider result.
That the proposed scenarios pass on the current build.
Mechanical correctness of combat, inventory, economy, character creation, equipment, or advancement.
That playability PASS and ATGB acceptability are the same judgment.
That deterministic host behavior is natural conversational competence.
That the PR-BL session orientation and later PR-EG history agree.
recommended_next_step: Stop. Review the design package before any runner, scoring sheet, fixture split, or production change. Do not report an ATGB result from this proposal. The fresh human playtest recorded in NEXT_SESSION remains the product step; this design does not replace it and does not start PR-BM.

supporting_files.why: Ten proposed conversations, 37 scored turns, facts, and pass criteria.
Existing chat, reset, telemetry, and evidence-packet reuse, and the small driver that would still be required after adoption.
ATGB governance. This proposal does not adopt a corpus and does not amend the standard.
Playability remains evaluate_playability. ATGB must not become a second scorer.
Points at the proposal and leaves the PR-BL versus PR-EG discrepancy unresolved.

self_contained_review_test: Not an automated gameplay bundle-only test. The ZIP packages the design, the catalog, and the feasibility note. It contains no gameplay transcript and claims no behavioral PASS.
